scope: Read-only primary-documentation/schema inspection of current standard Jupiter SwapV2 and PriceV3 REST interfaces. This is not a survey-proof that Jupiter has no private, separate, future or undocumented attestation product. No product policy selected or implemented.
observations: SwapV2 /build documents amounts, otherAmountThreshold, route instructions and blockhash metadata; no documented signature over quote values, oracle verification key or onchain quote-attestation verifier in this interface.

SwapV2 /order additionally documents optional serialized transaction, requestId, quoteId, maker and expireAt. quoteId/maker/expiry identify RFQ execution; signatureFeeLamports/signatureFeePayer describe transaction costs/payer, not a price signature. A transaction signature authorizes its message, not a general collateral-risk price.

PriceV3 documents createdAt, liquidity, usdPrice, blockId, decimals and priceChange24h, with no documented signed price payload/proof. blockId is nullable in the OpenAPI schema; createdAt means token creation, not price publication time.

Price docs derive reference USD price from the last swap, anchored on reliable oracle-priced tokens and filtered with liquidity, holder/trading/OrganicScore heuristics. Price updates follow swap activity rather than a fixed interval. Tokens can be omitted for reliability or no swap within7days; no null key is returned for omitted tokens.

PriceV3 reference spot USD value has no trade-size parameter and is not itself the all-in SOL cost to repurchase q after fees, impact and routing limits. It is useful input/display data but does not automatically implement the existing Bhat obligation.
engineering_inferences: Jupiter quotes can supply execution proposals and offchain pricing inputs. A program cannot authenticate arbitrary relayed JSON as Jupiter-origin data merely because it contains a route, quoteId, blockId or a borrower signature.

Using Jupiter-derived values in a signed onchain risk feed requires a separately specified trusted attester/oracle interface: configured keys/quorum, canonical mint/amount/currency/domain payload, observed time or slot and expiry, replay protection, freshness/deviation/failure rules, plus onchain verification. Signatures authenticate the attesters; they do not make manipulated data intrinsically fair.
Independent onchain pool pricing/guard bounds could be an alternative or additional check. No decision between those architectures is made by this review.

Successful atomic swap plus min-output and postbalance checks establishes what was actually exchanged. It does not prove route optimality, fair market price, robust liquidation valuation or resistance to a manipulated shallow pool.

qualification_to_prior_report.statement: Existing close accepts >=q, bounded spending and donated surplus. ExactIn is not inherently incompatible. Prior wording implying an unchanged exactly-q interface prevents integration is superseded. Remaining work is generic route authority/account validation, independently justified Bhat/risk pricing, and buyback/liquidation liveness.

no_attestation_documentation_claim_scope: Only the three currently inspected public standard response contracts; extra response properties may exist because schema absence is not a universal API nonexistence proof. No cryptographic signing service was discovered in inspected docs; obtain a specific signed-feed specification before claiming one is available.
